cases.name: each stage builds on the last

inputs.topic: why B-trees beat binary trees on disk

research.findings: B-trees have high fan-out, so fewer disk seeks.

critique.critique: I asserted fan-out without numbers, and never mentioned cache lines.

revise.final: B-trees have high fan-out (100+ keys per node), so a lookup costs far fewer disk seeks than a binary tree's one comparison per level. Cache-line behaviour matters too.

output.result: B-trees have high fan-out (100+ keys per node), so a lookup costs far fewer disk seeks than a binary tree's one comparison per level. Cache-line behaviour matters too.
